venue.name: Log Cabin Museum, Saanich Pioneer Society
venue.description: The Log Cabin Museum in Saanichton is owned and run by the Saanich Pioneer Society, a volunteer run registered charity. The cabin was built in 1933 and the museum describes itself as the oldest purpose built museum in BC still on its original site. It holds exhibits about the history of the Saanich Peninsula, including a permanent children's display, and is open to the public on Saturday afternoons with admission by donation. The Society says student classes and seniors' groups are encouraged to book a tour.
venue.address: 7910 Polo Park Cr, Saanichton BC V8M 2J4

facility_notes.washrooms: Washroom is very small but has grab bars.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Flat, paved parking lot, with 2 designated handicapped spots. Curb cut from parking lot to sidewalk. Ramp from paved sidewalk to entrance, slight doorsill.

restrictions: We welcome Guide and Service dogs, certified under the BC Guide Dog and Service Dog Act, with designated ID. All other dogs must remain outside.
venue.hours_notes: The Museum is open Saturdays 1-4pm (except Statutory holidays). The Archives is open for e-mail enquiries for the summer, and in person may be possible with prior arrangements.
venue.seasonal_notes: We are back to Spring/Summer hours, so we're open 1-4pm. We are closed some holiday weekends, so please check our calendar.

programs.name: Booked group tour of the Log Cabin
programs.description: The Society invites student classes and seniors' groups to book a tour of the Log Cabin. The museum is a single log building holding exhibits of local Saanich Peninsula history, with a permanent children's display and rotating exhibits. Admission to the museum is by donation. Nothing is published about what a booked tour costs, how long it runs, how many children can come, or which days tours are available.
programs.our_note: The museum is one small log building and its public hours are Saturday afternoons only, so a weekday visit has to be arranged with the volunteers who run it. No price, length, group size or minimum age is published, so ask for all four in the same call. The washroom is very small, which is worth knowing before you arrive with a group of little ones.
programs.practical_summary: There is a washroom on site and step free access by ramp from a flat paved parking lot, though the washroom is very small. Lunch space, bus parking, group size and the cost of a booked tour are not published, so it is worth a call.
programs.evidence: Student classes and seniors’ groups are encouraged to book a tour of the Log Cabin

images.alt: A single storey log building with a deep covered porch, a sign in the gable reading Log Cabin Museum, and both steps and a wooden ramp leading up to the entrance.

gaps: The cost of a booked group tour is not published. General museum admission is by donation, but nothing says whether a booked tour is treated the same way.
No minimum age is published, so it is not clear whether they take preschool and daycare groups as well as school classes.
No group size limit is published, and the building is small.
No length is published for a group tour.
How much notice they need for a booking is not published.
Public opening is Saturday afternoons only. Nothing says whether a group tour can be booked on a weekday.

No indoor lunch space is mentioned anywhere on the site, and there is nothing about bus parking or where a bus could drop off. The parking lot is described as flat and paved with two accessible spots.
No single booking route is given. The contact page offers a phone number and two general email addresses and says to use whichever suits, so the general enquiries address was recorded.
The Saanich Pioneer Society web address in our list redirects to logcabinmuseum.com, which is the same organisation's site.
No coordinates are published anywhere on the site, so only the address was recorded and the pin is left for geocoding later.
The main photograph carries a file name where its alt text should be, so the description of it was written after opening the image in a browser and looking at it.
